newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos has said he wants to be kept out of a growing debate between supporters and opponents of a move to extend his term beyong 1998. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- President Ramos has accepted the resignation of Justiniano C. Montano, deputy general manager for special projects of the Public Estates Authority, over a secretive visit to Thailand for negotiations with a Bangkok-based real estate firm. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Governor Nur Misuari of the Mindanao region is to address the Organisation of Islamic Conference foreign ministers' meet in Jakarta. (MANILA BULLETIN).

- The government will need to generate some 312 billion pesos in new investments to maintain the rate of growth in the economy, Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito F. Habito said in Tokyo. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Hottick Investment Ltd, a Hong Kong-based investment firm, has purchased the 75 percent holding in the National Steel Corp held by Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
- Philippine Airlines is likely to halve its $4.0 billion order for new aircraft from Airbus Industrie. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
